BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

## Threshold point: the "FINAL / settled at principal level" claim

The Seller says these positions were settled by both deal teams at principal level and shouldn't be re-opened. Nothing in our record supports that. Several Seller positions (20% / AUD 4.8M cap, 18-month period) match our conditional fallbacks, but those need prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. We should:

- Reply that nothing is agreed until the full SPA is settled.
- Confirm with Amelia Frost whether she agreed anything.
- Not treat the "market standard" preamble as a reason to move. It is the Seller's assertion, not evidence.

## Material departures from our playbook

### A. Liability architecture (highest priority)

| Issue | Seller position | Our position | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8M | Open at 25% / AUD 6M | 20% is a fallback we cannot use without Frost's written authority. Don't concede it. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. It would exclude many small claims. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher and a deductible rather than a tipping basket. The combined effect materially erodes recoverable value. |
| Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval. |
| Fundamental / Title | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | "Administrative simplicity" would cap title at AUD 4.8M on a AUD 24M purchase and expire it in 18 months. Reject. |
| "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (12.3/13) | Blanket application | Separate categories, no hidden general-regime override | This is a drafting device that pulls Title, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and payment/covenant claims into the general limits. Reverse it so limits apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated. |
| Cls 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 | Limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | There is no fraud carve-out at all. This must be fixed to the maximum extent enforceable, and it isn't something we can trade away. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

- **Disclosure Letter 1.1 / 1.2 and Schedule 7:** these disclose the whole data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and public records generally. That is exactly the deemed-disclosure approach we reject. It would let the Seller neutralise warranties by pointing to any document in the room. We should require specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
- **Cl 8.3 buyer knowledge:** this excludes claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or could discover from the data room or public records. It is effectively a constructive-knowledge bar and compounds the general disclosure. Delete it. If a qualifier is ever needed, it must be limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Letter 1.4 (no admission):** this is acceptable as far as it goes. We should make clear it doesn't qualify the warranties or the specific indemnities.

### C. Closing deliverables and price mechanics

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6M FY26 revenue, about 30%)**
- The Seller's own letter (item 2) admits there is no final written consent and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- The Seller proposes reasonable endeavours, with the consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.
- We should require an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a condition precedent in our favour. Reasonable endeavours alone is not enough for a customer of this size, and "on delivery" ignores whether the consent is conditional or effective.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2M)**
- The Seller admits the facility hasn't been repaid and there is no discharge of security (letter item 3). Its proposal is a post-Completion release.
- We should require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion (including PPSR and any other registered security).
- A post-completion release is available only against an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. We should not offer it now. This also matters for the debt-free/cash-free basis and the change-control clause 8.1.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)**
- The funds flow omits them, and the Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller", which is ambiguous.
- We should require either a specific funds-flow line item or an express seller-funded mechanism, with no silent exclusion.
- The Seller's letter (item 5) doesn't say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. We should ask the Seller to confirm which on-costs are triggered and who bears them. Don't assume a number.

### D. Specific matters

- **Ironquay IP:** the Seller says the indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, is adequate. We should broaden it, for example to ownership of and title to the SOW3 Project Materials, third-party and Ironquay claims, and related costs, while preserving the SOW3 cure (payment leading to transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3). The AUD 180,000 comes from DD-010 and is not independently verified (the Seller concedes this, letter item 4), so treat it as unconfirmed in either direction. Ask for payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment.
- **DD-006 export/privacy incident:** the Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". That is unsupported characterisation, and the letter itself says scope, access and notification are unknown. We shouldn't overreact either: assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way. Ask for log preservation, a documented investigation, regular updates, and cooperation. Reserve our position without asserting a breach.
- **Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate):** the Seller says "ordinary-course operating costs", but the letter (item 8) doesn't state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. We should assess from DD-008 and DD-011 and ask for the contract terms and timing. Don't accept the Seller's label, and don't treat the amount as Debt or deduct it from price automatically.
- **Tax and IP:** the Seller treats these as "settled under the general regime". They are open for us. Keep them as separate categories, and don't concede that they sit inside the general cap or time limits. We also shouldn't claim they are unlimited or resolved.
- **Title:** the Seller relies on the DD-012 register. That is a supplied internal source and not independent proof (the Seller's letter, item 10, acknowledges this). We should require independent evidence, such as ASIC extracts, share transfer and issue history, share certificates, board and shareholder authority, a PPSR/encumbrance search, and the Seller's capacity and authority.

### E. Lower-priority items

- **Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** the disclosures say neither appears to require consent for a share sale. These aren't in our playbook as issues, but we should verify against the underlying clauses rather than rely on the letter's summary. Note the lease notification obligation as a completion-timing item.

## Recommendations summary

1. **Don't accept "FINAL" status.** Respond that nothing is agreed until the whole SPA is settled. Check with Amelia Frost internally. Don't use the 20% / AUD 4.8M cap or the 18-month period without her written authority identifying the draft.
2. **Counter the general regime:** cap 25% / AUD 6M; de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 with first-dollar recovery; 24-month claims period.
3. **Create a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Fix the limitation drafting:** the limits apply only to general Warranty Claims, and Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories stay separate, with no blanket override.
5. **Add a fraud carve-out** for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance (cls 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).
6. **Replace deemed disclosure** with specific fair disclosure, and strike data-room, register and public-record disclosure.
7. **Delete cl 8.3.** Any fallback is limited to named seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and never covers title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
8. **Make Bluefen a condition:** effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
9. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release only against an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval.
10. **Bonuses:** a funds-flow line item or express seller funding for the AUD 420,000, plus triggered on-costs (the Seller to confirm which apply).
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and seek payment evidence and confirmatory assignment.
12. **DD-006:** covenants to preserve logs, investigate and update us. Make no assumption of a breach and no numeric demand.
13. **Sandbar:** diligence the terms. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
14. **Tax/IP:** keep them open and separate, and reject the "settled" characterisation.
15. **Title:** require independent evidence beyond the DD-012 register.

I can draft the cover response to Seller's counsel or a mark-up of the key clauses next. For anything that moves toward a fallback, I'd suggest preparing a short authority request for Amelia Frost first.
